source_text: ἐστι. Καὶ ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτὸ ὑμῖν ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἐξιλάσκεσθαι περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν· τὸ γὰρ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἀντὶ ψυχῆς ἐξιλάσεται. Διὰ τοῦτο εἴρηκα τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξ ὑμῶν οὐ φάγεται αἷμα. Καὶ ὁ προσήλυτος ὁ προσκείμενος ἐν ὑμῖν οὐ φάγεται αἷμα· καὶ ἄνθρωπος τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ἢ τῶν προσηλύτων τῶν προσκειμένων ἐν ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν θηρεύσῃ θήρευμα θηρίον ἢ πετεινὸν, ὃ ἐσθίεται, καὶ ἐκχεεῖ τὸ αἷμα, καὶ καλύψει αὐτὸ τῇ γῇ· ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πάσης σαρκὸς, αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐστι. Καὶ εἶπα τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Αἷμα πάσης σαρκὸς οὐ φάγεσθε, ὅτι ἡ ψυχὴ πάσης σαρκὸς αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐστι· πᾶς ὁ ἐσθίων αὐτὸ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν σαφῶς καὶ ἀναφανδὸν ὡς εἰς ψυχῆς τύπον τὸ αἷμα λαμβάνεται. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι, {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀλλοτριοῖ τοιγαροῦν ὁ νόμος, καὶ ὑπεξάγει σωμάτων τῶν σφαζομένων τὸ αἷμα, δόγμα διδάσκων ἀληθὲς, καὶ πρός γε ἡμῶν αὐτῶν ἐν πίστει δεκτὸν, καὶ ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις τίμιον, τὸ, ἀθάνατον εἶναί φημι, διακεῖσθαι καὶ φρονεῖν τὴν λογικὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ψυχὴν, ἣν τοῖς γηΐνοις σώμασιν, οὐ συγκαταφθείρει θάνατος, ἀπολύει δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ ἀνίησιν ὁ Δημιουργὸς, καὶ ὑπεξάγει τοῦ παθεῖν, ζωῆς ἀποφήνας μέτοχον. Πεποίηται γὰρ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐν ἀρχαῖς εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν, ἐνιέντος αὐτῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ πνοὴν ζωῆς· γέγραπται γὰρ ὡδί. Καταγράψομεν γὰρ, καθάπερ ἐγᾦμαι, τὸ ἄναλκι τῆς τὰ πάντα ζωογονούσης ζωῆς, εἰ τὸ πρὸς αὐτῆς γεγονὸς εἰς ζωὴν, συνδιόλλυσθαί φαμεν τοῖς προσκαίροις σώμασι. Συνέσει δὲ τῇ παγκάλῳ στέψομεν, ἀθάνατον εἶναι πιστεύοντες, δοκοῦν ὧδε ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῷ πάντων Δημιουργῷ, ἐν ᾧ ζῶμεν, καὶ κινούμεθα, καὶ ἐσμέν. Καὶ οὗτος, οἶμαί που, τῆς νομοθεσίας τῆς ἐπὶ τῷδε λόγος. Ἴωμεν δὲ καὶ ἐφ' ἕτερα δικαιώματα τῆς σκηνῆς. Ἔφη τοίνυν ὁ Θεὸς ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ, «Οὐ σφάξεις ἐπὶ ζύμῃ αἷμα θυσιάσματός μου.» Ἄζυμον ἔστω, φησὶ, τὸ προχεόμενον αἷμα, καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ προσκεκομισμένου εἰς θυσίαν τῷ Θεῷ, ζύμης αὐτῷ δηλονότι ἤτοι σεμιδάλεως ἐζυμωμένης, οὐκ ἐπενηνεγμένης· χρὴ γὰρ ἡμᾶς ἐκκεκαθαρμένους καὶ ἀζύμους ὥσπερ ὑπάρχοντας, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὴν ἐκ φαυλότητος καὶ πονηρίας οἱονεί πως ἐπιπλοκὴν, εἰς νοῦν οὐκ ἔχοντας, καθιεροῦν τῷ Θεῷ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ψυχὰς, ὧν εἰς τύπον τὸ αἷμα· νέον δὲ φύραμα καὶ ἀζύμους ἐκάλει καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, τοὺς εἰλικρινῆ καὶ ἀθόλωτον, καὶ ἀσυμμιγῆ φαυλότητος τὴν οἰκείαν τηροῦντας ψυχὴν, διὰ πίστεως δὲ δηλονότι τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν, καὶ ἀγάπης ὁλοτελοῦς. Ἀλλ' «Οὐδὲ μὴ κοιμηθῇ, φησὶ, στέαρ τῆς ἑορτῆς μου, ἕως πρωΐ,» τοῦτ' ἔστι, χθιζὸν οὐκ ἀνοίσεις στέαρ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας. Ἐν δὲ τῷ Λευιτικῷ σαφεστέραν ποιεῖται τοῦ νόμου τὴν δήλωσιν, καὶ τὸ χρῆμα ἐναργὲς καθίστησι λέγων περὶ τοῦ προσάγοντος θῦμα· «Κἂν εὐχὴν, ἢ ἑκούσιον θυσιάσῃ τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ, ᾗ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ προσενέγκῃ τὴν θυσίαν, βρωθήσεται, καὶ τῇ αὔριον· τὸ δὲ καταλειφθὲν ἀπὸ τῶν κρεῶν τῆς θυσίας, ἕως ἡμέρας τρίτης, ἐν πυρὶ καυθήσεται.
pass_a_gloss: [Completing Lev 17:11: '...is'.] And I have given (δίδωμι) it to you on the altar (θυσιαστήριον) to propitiate / make atonement (ἐξιλάσκομαι) for your souls; for its blood will make atonement in place of (ἀντί) soul. Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel: every soul of you shall not eat blood; and the proselyte residing among you shall not eat blood; and a man of the sons of Israel or of the proselytes residing among you who hunts (θηρεύω) game (θήρευμα), beast (θηρίον) or bird (πετεινόν) which is eaten, shall pour out the blood and cover (καλύπτω) it with earth; for the soul of all flesh is its blood. And I said to the sons of Israel: blood of all flesh you shall not eat, because the soul of all flesh is its blood; everyone eating it shall be utterly destroyed. Behold then clearly and openly (ἀναφανδόν) that the blood is taken into a type of soul. PALL: I understand. CYR: Therefore the law estranges (ἀλλοτριόω) and withdraws (ὑπεξάγω) the blood from the bodies slaughtered, teaching a true dogma (δόγμα ἀληθές), acceptable to us in faith and honored (τίμιον) in Churches: that, I mean, the rational soul (λογικὴ ψυχή) of the human is immortal (ἀθάνατος), is in a state (διάκειμαι) and thinks (φρονέω); which death does not destroy together (συγκαταφθείρω) with earthly bodies, but rather the Creator (Δημιουργός) releases (ἀπολύω) and lets go (ἀνίημι) and withdraws from suffering (ὑπεξάγει τοῦ παθεῖν), having shown it partaker (μέτοχος) of life. For the human was made in the beginning into a living soul (ψυχὴ ζῶσα), God sending into him breath of life (πνοὴ ζωῆς); for so it is written. For we shall record against (καταγράφω), as I think, weakness (τὸ ἄναλκι) of the Life that generates life for all (ζωογονέω), if we say that what came to be by it into life perishes together (συνδιόλλυμαι) with temporary (πρόσκαιρος) bodies. But with the all-beautiful understanding / wisdom (σύνεσις παγκάλη) we shall crown (στέφω) [it], believing [the soul] to be immortal, it seeming good that it be so to the Creator of all, in whom we live and move and are. And this, I think, is the reason (λόγος) of the legislation (νομοθεσία) on this. Let us go also to other ordinances (δικαιώματα) of the tent. God said then in Exodus: you shall not slaughter upon leaven (ζύμη) the blood of my sacrifice (θυσίασμα). Let the blood poured forth (προχέω) be unleavened (ἄζυμον), he says, and on behalf of what is brought for sacrifice to God, leaven clearly, or leavened fine flour (σεμίδαλις ἐζυμωμένη), not being brought upon it. For we must, being cleansed (ἐκκαθαίρω) and as it were unleavened, that is, not having in mind (εἰς νοῦν) the entanglement (ἐπιπλοκή) as it were from badness (φαυλότης) and wickedness (πονηρία), consecrate (καθιερόω) to God our own souls, of which the blood is into a type. And the divine (θεσπέσιος) Paul also called new lump (νέον φύραμα) and unleavened those keeping their own soul sincere (εἰλικρινής), unmuddied (ἀθόλωτος), and unmixed (ἀσυμμιγής) with badness, through faith into Christ and complete love (ἀγάπη ὁλοτελής). But 'neither shall the fat (στέαρ) of my feast (ἑορτή) sleep (κοιμάομαι) until morning', that is, you shall not offer up yesterday's (χθιζόν) fat for odor of fragrance. And in Leviticus he makes the declaration (δήλωσις) of the law clearer and sets the matter vivid, saying about the one bringing a victim: [Lev 7:16-17 LXX] if he sacrifices his gift as vow (εὐχή) or freewill (ἑκούσιον), on whatever day he offers the sacrifice it shall be eaten, and on the morrow (αὔριον); but what is left of the meats of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned in fire.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …And I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the soul. Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood, and the proselyte residing among you shall not eat blood. And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the proselytes residing among you, who takes in hunting a beast or a bird that may be eaten, shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth. For the soul of all flesh is its blood. And I said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the soul of all flesh is its blood; everyone who eats it shall be utterly destroyed’ (Leviticus 17:10–14). See, then, how clearly and openly the blood is taken as a type of the soul.

Cyril: The law, therefore, sets the blood apart and draws it away from the bodies of the slaughtered animals, teaching a true doctrine, one received by us in faith and held in honor in the Churches: I mean that the rational soul of man is immortal, and continues to exist and to think. Death does not destroy it together with earthly bodies; rather, the Creator releases it and sets it free, and exempts it from suffering, having made it a sharer in life. For in the beginning man was made a living soul, when God breathed into him the breath of life; for so it is written (Genesis 2:7). For, I think, we shall be charging the Life that gives life to all things with weakness if we say that what came into life from it perishes together with our temporary bodies. But we shall crown that Life with the most excellent wisdom if we believe that the soul is immortal, since the Creator of all, in whom we live and move and have our being (Acts 17:28), has willed that it be so. And this, I suppose, is the reason for the legislation on this point. But let us go on to other ordinances of the tent as well. God said, then, in Exodus: ‘You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leaven’ (Exodus 23:18). Let the blood that is shed be unleavened, he says, the blood shed for what has been brought to God as a sacrifice; that is, of course, no leaven, or fine flour that has been leavened, is to be brought with it. For we must be cleansed and, as it were, unleavened, that is, we must not harbor in our minds any entanglement, so to speak, with baseness and wickedness, and so consecrate to God our own souls, of which the blood is a type. And the inspired Paul also called those ‘a new batch’ and ‘unleavened’ (1 Corinthians 5:7–8) who keep their own soul sincere, unclouded and unmixed with baseness, through faith in Christ, of course, and through perfect love. But ‘neither shall the fat of my feast,’ he says, ‘remain overnight until morning’ (Exodus 23:18); that is, you shall not offer yesterday’s fat as a fragrant odor. And in Leviticus he sets out the law more clearly and makes the matter plain, saying of the one who brings a sacrifice (Leviticus 7:16–17): ‘If he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a freewill offering, on whatever day he offers his sacrifice it shall be eaten, and on the next day as well; but what is left of the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire…

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-quotation (Leviticus 17:11, after ἐστι); the inline reference (Leviticus 17:10–14) covers the whole quotation begun in section 24, as does the citation placed at its start in section 24. ψυχή is kept as 'soul' throughout the quotation because Cyril's argument turns on it (blood as type of the soul's immortality). ἀντὶ ψυχῆς rendered literally, 'in place of the soul'. διακεῖσθαι καὶ φρονεῖν is compressed and difficult; taken as 'continues in being and in understanding' (that the soul survives death in a conscious state). In 'we shall crown it with the most excellent wisdom' the object of στέψομεν is unexpressed; taken as the Life of the previous sentence (we honor that Life as supremely wise), parallel to 'charging the Life with weakness'; doubtful. τῆς ... ζωογονούσης ζωῆς is God, hence 'Life' capitalized. Genesis 2:7 is paraphrased, not quoted. Exodus 23:18 LXX: Οὐ θύσεις ἐπὶ ζύμῃ αἷμα θυσιάσματός μου, οὐδὲ μὴ κοιμηθῇ στέαρ τῆς ἑορτῆς μου ἕως πρωί; both halves are cited at their clauses (compare the parallel Exodus 34:25, not cited). The phrase ὑπὲρ τοῦ προσκεκομισμένου is taken as 'the blood shed for what has been brought to God as a sacrifice'. 1 Corinthians 5:7-8 supplies νέον φύραμα, ἄζυμοι and εἰλικρίνεια. The Leviticus 7:16-18 quotation continues into section 26. Exodus 23:18: Cyril has σφάξεις ('slaughter', the verb of Exodus 34:25) where LXX 23:18 has θύσεις; rendered 'offer', the usual English for this verse, since 'slaughter the blood' is not English; the rest of both halves matches 23:18. Cyril's 'Let the blood ... be unleavened' is his own paraphrase with φησί, so it carries no quotation marks.
